sections.title: Local remediation, why attention is expensive

keyTerms.definition: Grouped-query attention. Groups of query heads share KV heads, shrinking the cache with graceful quality loss.
Multi-head latent attention. It caches a low-rank latent per token instead of per-head keys and values.
Mixture of experts. The model owns many FFNs but routes each token to only k of them.
The stored keys and values that let decode skip recomputing attention over the past.
The aux loss that penalizes correlation between tokens sent to an expert and mean router probability.
A per-expert inbox size. Tokens beyond capacity are dropped and skip the expert.

recall.question: How do MHA, MQA, and GQA differ in KV cache size?
recall.answer: MHA gives every query head a private KV copy. MQA shares one copy across all heads. GQA shares per group, so the cache shrinks proportionally to sharing.

recall.question: Why does MoE scale parameters without scaling compute?
recall.answer: Parameters scale with the expert count E, but each token consults only k experts, so compute scales with k.

recall.question: What does linear attention trade away, and what does it gain?
recall.answer: It replaces softmax with a feature map, turning attention into an RNN with a matrix-valued hidden state. Cost drops to O(T*dh^2), but the kernel must stay positive and faithful.
